name: Varan Bhaat
subtitle: plain toor dal with ghee and a touch of jaggery over hot rice, the first course of every festive meal

ingredients.note: use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free
half in the dal, half poured over the rice

ingredients.qty: 700ml for the dal, 600ml for the rice

prepNotes: Rinse the dal in three changes of water until it runs clear, then soak 20 minutes so it cooks evenly.
Rinse and soak the rice 15 minutes as well; varan bhaat is eaten with soft, loose grains.
Varan carries no onion, garlic or chilli by design. Do not be tempted to improve it.

steps.text: Rinse and soak the toor dal 20 minutes, then drain.
Pressure cook the dal with 500ml water and the turmeric for 4 whistles, or simmer covered 40 minutes, until it collapses at a touch.
Cook the rice in the remaining water until soft, about 15 minutes, and keep it covered and hot.
Open the cooker and whisk the dal smooth with a ladle, adding the remaining 200ml water until it pours easily.
steps.tip: Varan should be thin enough to soak into rice, not thick enough to stand a spoon in.

steps.text: Bring it back to a simmer with the salt, jaggery and hing and cook 5 minutes.
steps.tip: The jaggery is not there to sweeten it, only to round the edge. Two teaspoons is plenty.

steps.text: Heat the ghee, crackle the cumin seeds if using, and pour it into the dal.
Squeeze in the lemon off the heat and taste for salt.
Serve a ladle of varan over a mound of hot rice with a spoon of raw ghee on top, and eat it first, before anything else on the plate.

storage: The varan keeps 3 days refrigerated and thickens; loosen with hot water and re-season. Cooked rice keeps 2 days. Steam it back to life rather than microwaving it dry.

nutrition.method: Estimated from raw ingredients using USDA FoodData Central. Cooking losses are not modelled and added salt is excluded, so sodium is not given.
